<p class="page-deck">The lab studies how urban climate knowledge becomes cumulative: what may be useful across places, where new evidence would matter, how action becomes operable, and what changes for people and places.</p>

::: {.notice}
**One connected programme.** The themes are ordered questions, not independent subject areas. Consequences generate new evidence, revise judgements and shape what cities investigate next. Projects may enter the cycle at different points.
:::

[Read our approach to evidence, relevance, use, delivery and consequences →](/research/our-approach.html)

{{< include generated/research-themes.qmd >}}

## Research facets, not competing themes

Climate domains such as mitigation and adaptation; empirical sectors such as buildings, transport, energy, food, heat and housing; geographies such as British Columbia, Canada and the United Kingdom; and methods such as comparative research, synthesis, modelling and data visualisation remain separately tagged. They support the four research themes rather than define the lab's public identity.
